title: What is known about 1RB1RF_1RC0RE_1LD0RB_1RE0LC_1RA0LE_0RC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RF_1RC0RE_1LD0RB_1RE0LC_1RA0LE_0RC---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Past a fixed prefix the tape is a queue of blocks (01)^k with sizes 4j - 2; a cursor eats one block a copy at a time and rebuilds it at the right end (proved in Lean). The order in which blocks are fed is not understood yet.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 77,847 cells have been visited and 38,670 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.559).

claims.title: Tape structure
claims.text: After a fixed prefix (101001100)^128 (10)^10 0110, the tape is a list of blocks (01)^k separated by 00110. The exponents that persist are 14, 62, 254, 1022, 4094, that is 4j − 2, each four times the previous plus 6. At 109 steps the list reads 14, 61, 62×313, 9, 213, 254×61, 1300, 196; near the right end blocks are being rebuilt with the next larger size, as in a counter in base 4.

claims.title: The feeding rules
claims.text: Fd c k m L = L (01)^k c (01)^m 0 B> 0^inf: one visit of the right end takes Fd 0 (k+1) m to Fd 1 k (m+2) (4m+18 steps) and Fd 1 (k+1) m to Fd 0 k (m+2) (4m+10 steps), for all k, m and every tape L; two visits take Fd 0 (k+2) m to Fd 0 k (m+4) in 8m+36 steps, iterated in feeds.

claims.title: A queue of blocks of size 4^j - 2
claims.text: Past a fixed prefix the tape is a list of blocks (01)^k separated by 00110, the persistent sizes 14, 62, 254, 1022, 4094 (each 4k+6); a cursor near the right end eats a block one copy at a time and rebuilds it at the end, like a counter.

claims.title: No halt in the first 4.61×10<sup>14</sup> steps of an accelerated run
claims.text: Observed, not proved: the accelerated simulator rsim.py ran 4.61×1014 steps from blank tape without reaching a halting transition. Its tape, state and head position were equal to those of a plain C simulator at 6 checkpoints, the last at 1.06×1010 steps. Of these steps, the part after the last checkpoint rests on the simulator alone, including 1,717 trip-level jumps: a jump applies many identical round trips at once after seeing the same tape shape recur with constant count changes, which is validated against direct simulation but not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Missing: the rules when a block is used up and the global schedule of the queue; see Next steps in the README.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LE_1RC0LB_1RD1RF_1RE0RB_1LA0RD_0RE--- up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LE_1LC0RA_1LD0RC_1LE1LF_1LA0LC_0LA--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 77,847 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).
No halt in the accelerated simulator (observed, not proved; checked against direct simulation up to 1.06×10<sup>10</sup> steps).

sections.heading: Blocks eaten one piece at a time and rebuilt at the end
html: Write a for 01 and b for 00110. Past a fixed prefix, the tape is a list of blocks of a's separated by b's, with sizes 14, 62, 254, 1022, 4094 (each four times the previous plus 6):

Near the right end a cursor cell c (0 or 1) separates the block being eaten from the block being built. Every time the head reaches the right end, one 01 leaves the block before the cursor, two join the block at the end, and the cursor flips. This is proved in Lean for blocks of any size.

<svg viewBox='0 0 560 110' role='img' aria-label='one copy leaves the block left of the cursor, two join the end block' style='width:100%;max-width:560px;height:auto;font:12px var(--mono)'><rect x='10' y='15' width='200' height='22' fill='var(--ink)'/><text x='110' y='30' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--bg)'>a^(k+1)</text><rect x='214' y='15' width='8' height='22' fill='var(--head)'/><text x='218' y='52' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--muted)'>0</text><rect x='226' y='15' width='120' height='22' fill='var(--accent)'/><text x='286' y='30' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--bg)'>a^m</text><rect x='10' y='70' width='188' height='22' fill='var(--ink)'/><text x='104' y='85' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--bg)'>a^k</text><rect x='202' y='70' width='8' height='22' fill='var(--head)'/><text x='206' y='107' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--muted)'>1</text><rect x='214' y='70' width='144' height='22' fill='var(--accent)'/><text x='286' y='85' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--bg)'>a^(m+2)</text></svg>

The runs of equal blocks behave like the digits of a counter. The machine 1RB1RF_0RC0RE_0RD1RA_1LE0LA_1LB0LD_0RD--- runs the same kind of queue with sizes 4j. What is missing is the schedule (which block is fed next, and when), so there is no closed rule yet and no answer about halting.

Where it could halt

Only when, in state A, the head reads a 1 and steps right onto another 1, with 111 just to its left; the words of the queue never contain 111.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.559).
After 109 steps the tape spans 77,847 cells (1,575 left of the start, 49,217 right), with a density of 1s of 0.497.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0LE_1LC0RA_1LD0RC_1LE1LF_1LA0LC_0LA---: rename A→D, B→E, C→A, D→B, E→C, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state C, in a mirror

summary: A queue of blocks (01)^k with sizes 4^j - 2, eaten one copy at a time at a cursor and rebuilt at the right end, like a counter; the feeding rules are proved in Lean; open.
